paragraphs.text: A **cash-secured put** is a short put position in which the writer sets aside enough cash to buy the shares at the strike price if the put is assigned [S1]. The writer sells the put, collects the premium up front, and accepts the obligation to buy 100 shares per contract at the strike any time before expiration [S1]. The word *secured* refers to the cash: in a cash account the broker holds the full purchase price as collateral for the whole life of the trade [S1]. A **naked put** is the same contract, but in a margin account the broker holds only a **margin requirement**, a fraction of the purchase price computed under exchange and FINRA minimum rules, and the writer keeps the rest of their buying power free for other positions [S4].

This run allocated {{allocation.csp_pct|pct}} to cash-secured puts, {{allocation.leaps_pct|pct}} to LEAPS, and {{allocation.cash_pct|pct}} to cash under a {{regime.label}} regime with a risk-free rate of {{regime.risk_free_rate_pct|pct}}. The good-to-own quality gate passed {{quality_screen.passed_count}} underlyings ({{quality_screen.passed_tickers|list}}) and excluded none.

The quality gate is a **filter, not a discovery engine**: it decides which tickers are allowed into the option screeners at all, records a reason for every rejection, and produces a score for the survivors [S5]. The product promise is "stocks you would be happy to own if assigned" [S5].

The trend board is a secondary signal only. The top trend candidates ({{trends[0].ticker}}, {{trends[1].ticker}}, {{trends[2].ticker}}) were all skipped because they are not on the good-to-own list, as recorded in the errors.

The bottleneck board is also a secondary signal: it re-orders quality-gated stocks, never adds one. The highest-scoring layer is {{bottlenecks.layers[0].name}} at {{bottlenecks.layers[0].score}}, with thesis state {{bottlenecks.layers[0].thesis_state}}.

Two positions were sized. {{positions[0].candidate_id}} has a breakeven of {{positions[0].payoff.breakeven|money}}, a maximum loss of {{positions[0].payoff.max_loss|money}}, and a realistic loss of {{positions[0].realistic_loss|money}}. {{positions[1].candidate_id}} has a breakeven of {{positions[1].payoff.breakeven|money}}, a maximum loss of {{positions[1].payoff.max_loss|money}}, and a realistic loss of {{positions[1].realistic_loss|money}}.

A **poor man's covered call** is a two-leg position: a long, deep in-the-money LEAPS call and a short, near-term, out-of-the-money call on the same stock [S3]. Formally it is a **long call diagonal spread**: different strikes and different expirations [S3]. **Assignment** is the process by which an option writer is selected to fulfil the obligation of a contract that a holder has exercised [S2].

The risk picture shows {{risk.checks_passed}} of {{risk.checks_total}} checks passed. A {{risk.stress[0].shock}} move with a {{risk.stress[0].iv_shock}} IV shock gives {{risk.stress[0].pnl|money}}, and a {{risk.stress[2].shock}} move with a {{risk.stress[2].iv_shock}} IV shock gives {{risk.stress[2].pnl|money}}.
